open_questions: Is the 485 ppm secondary at phase 0.782 a true eclipse/reflection or a spot artifact synchronized to the variable rotation? High-resolution photometry or radial velocities will test eccentricity/shape.

Is the sector-to-sector depth change (1582 vs 656 ppm) caused by unocculted spots/detrending on this highly variable star or by a blended/background source with sector-dependent dilution? Multi-color transit photometry and centroid localization will test.
Does the RUWE 2.469 high astrometric excess indicate an unseen bound companion that could produce the secondary signal alongside a planet? Additional Gaia astrometry is needed.
dossier.public_summary: A 14-day flat-bottomed dip about 1054 ppm is consistent with a 2.8 Earth-radius planet on a K dwarf, and shows no odd-even difference and a duration that fits the star. The star is highly spotted and shows depth that changes from 1582 ppm to 656 ppm between sectors and a possible shallow secondary dip, with no clear centroid image. Those systematics make a planet possible but not clearly favoured over a blended or variable-star mimic. Extra ground-based photometry and radial velocities are needed to confirm which effect is real.

reasons.why: Depth changes by 82% between sectors with p_constant 0.0007625; sector_depths_by_source verdict changes_within_a_source p_constant 0.0007603821996182816 confirms real change within SPOC, not calibration. Many planets show sector changes from aperture, but this magnitude requires explanation.
reasons.value: p_constant 0.0007625, depth_change_pct 82.75, sector55 1582+/-246 ppm vs sector82 656+/-123 ppm

reasons.why: Nominal depth is planet-like (rp_rearth 2.846, shape v_sigma -1.415 flat), but a 485 ppm secondary at phase 0.782 is ~46% of primary and snr near only slightly below the best 5.459 brightening. Phase offset 0.282 suggests it is not at half-orbit, but the signal is not clearly detached. If real, it favours a stellar companion over a planet; if artifact, planets remain possible.
reasons.value: snr 4.914, depth 485 ppm, depth_over_dip 0.4604, phase 0.782, best_brightening_snr 5.459

reasons.why: Star is strongly spotted (amplitude >> depth 1054 ppm, ruwe 2.469) and period ratio ~2.56 is non-integer. Phase_curve amplitude 83.75 ppm ratio_to_depth 0.0795 and chi2 4.835/9 shows no strong phase modulation, so spots alone do not explain the depth change or secondary, but they strongly contribute to systematics and inflate odd_even diff_sigma 2.158 and the suspect secondary.
reasons.value: rotation 5.475 d, amplitude 3287 ppm sector55 and 1536 ppm sector82, signal_over_rotation 2.560949771689498

reasons.why: Machine scorer trained on followed-up candidates ranks this well below the median planet (0.5), consistent with the combination of sector depth instability, high-amplitude variability, and ambiguous secondary. This supports flagging over a confident gate2.
